items.title: Desktop chat scrollbar jumps backward every few seconds
items.body:
# Desktop chat scrollbar jumps backward every few seconds

  ## Summary
  When reading the end of a conversation in the Hermes Desktop app, the chat viewport's scrollbar periodically jumps
  backward by a few pixels (sometimes 50+ px). The user is at the bottom of the latest message, then the scroll position
  suddenly shifts upward as if the page scrolled up on its own. Browser console repeatedly logs `ResizeObserver loop
  completed with undelivered notifications`.

  ## Environment
  - **App**: Hermes Desktop (official release, freshly installed)
  - **OS**: Windows 11 (Chinese locale; `PYTHONIOENCODING` and console encoding aside, the renderer issue reproduces
  regardless of locale)
  - **Renderer**: Electron (Chromium)
  - **Provider in use during repro**: irrelevant to the bug — it reproduces with no LLM streaming (idle conversation), so
  it is not token-rendering specific

  ## Reproduction
  1. Open any conversation with at least 10 messages (or a single very long message).
  2. Stay at the bottom of the conversation for 30+ seconds. Do not scroll.
  3. Observe the scrollbar position.
  4. Every few seconds the scrollbar jumps backward. The just-visible content at the bottom appears to shift up by a few
  to several dozen pixels.

  This also reproduces with the existing repro script: see `apps/desktop/scripts/measure-jump.mjs` (referenced in
  `useThreadScrollAnchor` comments). The maintainers already know the underlying mechanism — `distFromBottom 0 → 49 within
   one frame, sticking forever`.

  ## Expected
  The scroll position should stay at the bottom (or wherever the user left it) when the user is not actively scrolling.
  The auto-stick-to-bottom behavior should not be observable as a backward jump.

  ## Actual
  - The `pinToBottom` callback in `useThreadScrollAnchor`
  (`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread-virtualizer.tsx:198-209`) sets `el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight`.
  - The `ResizeObserver` in the same file (lines ~299-329) fires the pin on every size change of the scroller and of its
  first child.
  - The ResizeObserver fires faster than `pinToBottom` can re-pin: the new `scrollHeight` is read in the same frame the
  layout actually settles, but the browser has already delivered an interim `scroll` event whose `scrollTop` is now lower
  than `lastTopRef.current` from the previous frame.
  - That interim scroll event passes the disarm condition at line 261 (`if (top + 1 < lastTopRef.current)`), which clears
  `armedRef.current = false`.
  - With sticky-bottom disarmed, the user-visible result is a one-frame jump in the negative scroll direction (sometimes
  `49px` per the maintainers' own measurement).
  - Renderer console (visible in `desktop.log`):
    ```
    [hermes] [renderer console] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
    ```

  ## Trigger sources
  Anything that causes the scroller or its content to resize:
  - Streaming LLM tokens (most common during active responses)
  - Virtualized item measurement (`useVirtualizer` calling `measureElement` on first render of an item)
  - Composer height changes (e.g., suggestion chips appearing, the completion drawer opening, queued-message indicator)
  - Code-block syntax highlighting re-tokenization (Streamdown / Shiki) inside an already-rendered message

  The bug is **not** specific to streaming — it reproduces on a static conversation as soon as the virtualizer decides to
  measure an item it hadn't measured before.

  ## Suggested fix directions
  1. The disarm condition is too eager. The 1px threshold on `scrollTop` is fragile because the same frame that delivers a
   smaller `scrollTop` may not be user-driven — it can be the browser's interim layout pass. Consider only disarming on
  `wheel` / `touchmove` (already wired) and on `scroll` events whose `scrollTop` change cannot be explained by a
  `pinToBottom` write in the same frame.
  2. The ResizeObserver should observe **the content height only**, not the scroller. The scroller's own resize fires on
  window resize and other non-content-driven events and triggers spurious pins.
  3. Coalescing by rAF is good but insufficient when several ResizeObserver entries fire in the same frame after the rAF
  callback has already run. Consider a `setTimeout(0)` or `MessageChannel` post-rAF pass, or a microtask scheduled from
  the rAF.
  4. Before writing `el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight`, double-check that the user was actually at-bottom (or close) and
  that the change is not the result of content height shrinking (in which case the user's intended view is preserved, not
  re-pinned).

  ## Workaround (user-side, until fixed)
  - Use the TUI (`hermes` CLI) — no virtualized scroll, no jump.
  - None found in the desktop app. `overflow-anchor: none` injected via DevTools does **not** resolve it (the bug is in
  the React pin logic, not the browser's scroll-anchor algorithm).

  ## Severity
  - Affects every desktop user.
  - Frequency: every few seconds under typical use.
  - Not data-corrupting but severely degrades readability of long sessions.

# Hermes Agent Bug Report — TUI Status Bar Reads Alias `context_length` Instead of Active Model

**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Severity:** Low (display only; actual context window is honored server-side)
**Component:** CLI TUI / status bar
**Affects:** Anyone using `model_aliases` with a custom `context_length`

---

## Summary

The CLI status bar's context-window meter shows the `context_length` value from a `model_aliases.<persona>.context_length` block instead of the active `model.context_length` from `config.yaml`, causing the user to see a stale or persona-specific number that does not match the true working context window.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `model.default: minimax/minimax-m3` with `model.context_length: 1048576` (1M) in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
2. Also define a `model_aliases` block, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   model_aliases:
     sophia-cloud:
       model: minimax/minimax-m2.7
       provider: openrouter
       context_length: 204800
   ```

3. Launch `hermes` (interactive CLI) and load the active m3 model
4. Observe the status bar's context meter

## Expected Behavior

Status bar shows `model.context_length: 1048576` (1M tokens) for the active model — or, if the provider's server-side cap is lower (which is the case here, see below), the real API cap (524,288 for m3 on OpenRouter as of 2026-06-03).

## Actual Behavior

Status bar shows `204800` (200K) — exactly matching `model_aliases.sophia-cloud.context_length`, even though the active model is m3 (not m2.7) and is not routed through the `sophia-cloud` alias.

This is reproducible with a persona-style alias like `sophia-cloud` or any other alias whose `context_length` differs from the active model's.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The TUI status bar appears to be reading from `model_aliases.<persona>.context_length` first, falling back to `model.context_length` only if no alias is defined. With a named persona active, the alias value wins regardless of which model is actually being served. (Not a hard confirmation — code in `hermes_cli/commands.py` / status-bar render path would pin it down.)

## Related Issue (for context)

This is the bug; the *trigger* is that `minimax/minimax-m3` advertises 1M context on the dev page but OpenRouter's `top_provider.context_length` is `524288` (512K). So even with the alias leak fixed, the meter will show 1M while the API silently caps at 512K. Possible follow-on bugs:

- The status bar should query the provider's `/models` endpoint (or use the response's `usage` payload) to display the *real* server cap, not the locally-configured `context_length`.
- `config.yaml`'s `model.context_length` should be validated against the provider's actual cap on session start, with a warning logged if it overshoots.

## Environment

- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) on Windows 11
- Hermes version: v0.15.2
- Active model: `minimax/minimax-m3` via OpenRouter
- OpenRouter API returns `top_provider.context_length: 524288` for m3 (verified 2026-06-03)
- Other `model_aliases` defined: `sophia-cloud` (m2.7, 204800), `sophia-local` (qwen3.5:9b, 65536)

## Workaround Until Fixed

Set `model.context_length` to match the actual server cap of the active model. For m3 on OpenRouter, that's `524288`. The TUI will then show the real window.

## Suggested Fix Direction

In the TUI status-bar render code (likely in `hermes_cli/commands.py` or the Ink-based renderer), the context-meter source should be resolved in this priority order:

1. `model.context_length` from the active model block (always wins for non-aliased models)
2. Provider's API-reported cap (preferred — reflects actual server limits)
3. `model_aliases.<persona>.context_length` only when the active model IS the alias's model

A short-circuit where the persona alias overrides the active model — even when the alias targets a *different* model — is the bug to remove.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Node.js: v22.16.0
- Hermes: main branch, commit `e114b31edaec`
- Install method: PowerShell bootstrap installer

## What happened
Installer crashes at stage **desktop** (Electron/Vite build). Reproducible on retry — all prior stages (uv, python, git, node, system-packages, repository, venv, dependencies, node-deps) succeed.

## Error
```
Error: Cannot find module '@rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc'
    at requireNative (rolldown/dist/shared/binding-BeU_1iEk.mjs:507)
    ...
    code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

The `rolldown` bundler (used by Vite) cannot find its native Windows binding. The error message itself references [npm/cli#4828](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828) — a known npm bug with optional native dependencies.

## Workaround
```powershell
cd apps/desktop
Remove-Item -Recurse node_modules, package-lock.json -Force
cd ..
npm install
npm run build
```
Then re-run the installer — earlier stages are skipped, picks up from desktop.

## Suggested fix
The installer's desktop build step could detect this npm bug on Windows and automatically clear `node_modules` + `package-lock.json` before retrying, or use `npm install --force` to ensure optional native bindings are installed.

Attached below (username redacted).

items.body:
### Bug Description

The Hermes Desktop app (Electron) on a **native Linux Wayland session** has persistent periodic flickering/jumping of the chat transcript — both during streaming and while idle. The content jumps up/down every few seconds, making it difficult to read long responses.

This is a **native Wayland** session (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland), **not** SSH-forwarded, VNC, RDP, or WSLg. The fix in PR #37932 (commit `6a2909fe5`) only addresses remote/forwarded displays and does not help here.

The scroll-logic patches from issue #37549 (programmaticScrollPendingRef counter + flushPendingViewState guard) improved the situation marginally but the flickering persists.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Desktop on a native Wayland Linux desktop
2. Start a chat session with a long response
3. Observe periodic flickering / jumping of the transcript, worse during streaming

### Expected Behavior

Smooth, stable rendering of the chat transcript with no periodic visual jumping.

### Actual Behavior

Chat content jumps up and down periodically, scroll position is lost or reset, making it hard to read through responses.

### Attempted Workarounds (all ineffective)

1. `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU=1` (force software rendering) — no improvement
2. `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=x11` (force X11 backend) — no improvement
3. Native Wayland Ozone via `ELECTRON_EXTRA_LAUNCH_ARGS="--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland"` — no improvement
4. Manual scroll-anchor patches from #37549 (clear pending ref in disarm(), cap counter at 1, guard setMessages on no-change) — slight improvement but flicker remains
5. The upstream remote-display detection (commit `6a2909fe5`) only helps remote/forwarded sessions (SSH, VNC, RDP, WSLg) — not applicable to native Wayland

### Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.17.0-35-generic x86_64
- **Display server**: Wayland (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland)
- **Hermes version**: v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)
- **Electron**: ^40.9.3
- **Desktop build commit**: e114b31ed (includes PR #37932 fixes)

### Related

- #37549 — same flicker pattern reported on macOS (two root causes found, partially overlapping)
- #37893 — high Renderer CPU + flickering on macOS (open, root cause not identified)
- #37203 — Wayland WebGL glyph atlas corruption (dashboard terminal, different from desktop chat)

### Proposed Fix

The issue appears to be an Electron/Chromium GPU compositor problem on native Wayland. Possible approaches:

1. Detect native Wayland sessions similarly to how remote displays are detected in `bootstrap-platform.cjs`, and disable hardware acceleration for Wayland sessions that exhibit the issue
2. Upgrade Electron to a version with better Wayland GPU compositing support
3. Implement a render-throttling mechanism to reduce repaint frequency during streaming

Happy to provide additional debug info or run diagnostic scripts.

# fix(mcp): pin optional catalog installs before bootstrap

## Severity Assessment
### CVSS Assessment

| Metric | v3.1 | v4.0 |
|--------|------|------|
| **Score** | 9.6 / 10.0 | 9.4 / 10.0 |
| **Severity** | Critical | Critical |
| **Vector** | CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L | CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:L |
| **Calculator** | [CVSS v3.1 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L) | [CVSS v4.0 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:L) |

### Threat Model Alignment
Hermes `SECURITY.md` section 2 treats operator-approved optional MCP catalog entries as trusted installation inputs. This is `SECURITY.md` section 3.1 `Trust-model documentation violations` because a catalog manifest can name a floating git ref that later executes attacker-controlled bootstrap code inside the agent environment.

## Impact
The in-repo optional MCP catalog is presented as Nous-reviewed, but install flow accepts catalog refs that are not immutable SHAs. A later force-push or branch update can make a trusted catalog entry clone and run attacker-controlled bootstrap code with access to the operator's Hermes environment and credentials.

## Affected Component
**File:** `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py:82-92`

```python
@dataclass
class InstallSpec:
    """Optional bootstrap step (git clone + dep install).

    Omit for one-shot launchable servers (npx, uvx).
    """
    type: str  # "git"
    url: str
    ref: str  # commit/tag/branch — pinned, never floats
    bootstrap: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

```

Secondary paths:

optional-mcps/n8n/manifest.yaml:26-35

## Technical Reproduction
1. Use Hermes Agent latest upstream `main` at source receipt commit `e114b31edaec8588e085e6748582672356529170`.
2. Inspect the optional MCP manifest and confirm the catalog entry uses a floating git ref rather than an immutable commit SHA.
3. Confirm `mcp_catalog.py` clones and bootstraps the referenced repository during optional MCP install.
4. Replace or advance the floating upstream ref with a bootstrap that writes a local marker or reads environment metadata.
5. Run the optional MCP install path and observe bootstrap execution from the floating ref; expected result is refusal before clone/bootstrap.

## Demonstrated Impact
- Catalog trust is attached to the manifest, but executed code is resolved later from a mutable git reference.
- Bootstrap runs inside the Hermes agent environment where operator credentials may be available.

## Environment
Hermes latest-main source receipt: `e114b31edaec8588e085e6748582672356529170` on current `main`. Runtime prerequisite: optional MCP install flow for the catalog entry with a floating git ref. Redaction complete; no secrets, tokens, private logs, or unrelated local paths are included. Public route status: public issue plus linked review-ready PR through `public_security_full_disclosure`; redaction checked.
Source freshness receipt: `source_ready` for `upstream-main` at `e114b31edaec8588e085e6748582672356529170` via `/tmp/hermes-source-receipt.json`; affected paths exist in the prepared latest-main checkout.

## Remediation Advice
Require optional MCP catalog `install.ref` values to be immutable commit SHAs before cloning or bootstrapping, and fail closed with clear remediation text when a catalog entry uses a branch, tag, or other floating ref.

items.title: Discord interaction buttons can expire while still appearing actionable
items.body:
## Bug description

Discord interactive prompts are very useful, but the response window appears to be too short for async usage.

When Hermes asks for user input through Discord interaction buttons, clicking a button after some delay can fail with Discord's generic error:

> Interaction failed

The original prompt message is still visible and still appears actionable, but the button click no longer works.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Trigger a Hermes prompt in Discord that asks the user to choose between multiple buttons.
2. Wait long enough before answering. Exact timeout not measured.
3. Click one of the visible buttons.

## Actual behavior

Discord displays:

> Interaction failed

No fallback path is obvious from the message.

## Expected behavior

Hermes should handle expired Discord interactions gracefully instead of leaving buttons that appear usable but fail.

Possible improvements:

- Keep Discord components valid longer when possible.
- Disable or visually expire buttons after the interaction timeout.
- Edit the message to say the prompt expired.
- Allow the user to answer by replying with text after buttons expire.
- Add a configurable timeout for Discord input interactions.
- On expired interaction, re-open the same question automatically or provide a retry path.

## Impact

Discord interactions are a great UX improvement, especially for quick choices, but users often do not answer immediately in async conversations. If the interaction expires too aggressively, the feature becomes unreliable.

### Threat Model Alignment
Hermes `SECURITY.md` section 2 treats remote terminal backends as isolation boundaries for LLM-emitted shell and file operations. This is `SECURITY.md` section 3.1 `OS-level isolation escape` because `sync_back` can copy attacker-controlled remote files into mapped host skill directories during backend cleanup.

## Impact
Remote backend cleanup downloads the remote `.hermes/` tree and copies modified mapped files, plus new files under mapped parent directories, into the host `~/.hermes/` tree. A malicious remote task can persist files into host skill directories and defeat the operator's chosen terminal-backend isolation.

## Affected Component
**File:** `tools/environments/file_sync.py:370-402`

```python

                if applied:
                    logger.info("sync_back: applied %d changed file(s)", applied)
                else:
                    logger.debug("sync_back: no remote changes detected")

    def _resolve_host_path(self, remote_path: str,
                           file_mapping: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None) -> str | None:
        """Find the host path for a known remote path from the file mapping."""
        mapping = file_mapping if file_mapping is not None else []
        for host, remote in mapping:
            if remote == remote_path:
                return host
        return None

    def _infer_host_path(self, remote_path: str,
                         file_mapping: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None) -> str | None:
        """Infer a host path for a new remote file by matching path prefixes.

        Uses the existing file mapping to find a remote->host directory
        pair, then applies the same prefix substitution to the new file.
        For example, if the mapping has ``/root/.hermes/skills/a.md`` →
        ``~/.hermes/skills/a.md``, a new remote file at
        ``/root/.hermes/skills/b.md`` maps to ``~/.hermes/skills/b.md``.
        """
        mapping = file_mapping if file_mapping is not None else []
        for host, remote in mapping:
            remote_dir = str(Path(remote).parent)
            if remote_path.startswith(remote_dir + "/"):
                host_dir = str(Path(host).parent)
                suffix = remote_path[len(remote_dir):]
                return host_dir + suffix
        return None
```

Secondary paths:

tools/environments/daytona.py:182-196
tools/environments/modal.py:369-378
tools/environments/ssh.py:253-262

## Technical Reproduction
1. Use Hermes Agent latest upstream `main` at source receipt commit `46ea0a184dd461fd09bd30acfe2bde35f27924d4`.
2. Enable a remote backend such as Daytona, Modal, or SSH with file sync enabled for the Hermes home tree.
3. Create a new remote file under a mapped host skill-directory parent path during the remote task.
4. Let backend cleanup invoke `sync_back` before the remote environment is stopped or deleted.
5. Observe the remote-created file copied into the host skill directory; expected result is no implicit host persistence without an explicit allowlist.

## Demonstrated Impact
- `sync_back` infers host paths for new remote files under mapped parents.

- `schtasks /create /ru SYSTEM` also fails with access denied

4. → UnauthorizedAccessException

User-scope environment variable writes should work for admin users.

`install.ps1` should detect this condition and fall back to one of:
1. Launching `sysdm.cpl` or `rundll32 sysdm.cpl,EditEnvironmentVariables` so the user can set vars via the GUI
2. Using `reg.exe` via a scheduled task running as SYSTEM (if schtasks works)
3. Printing the required environment variables and asking the user to set them manually
4. Using `setx` command which may bypass the .NET restriction (untested)

- OS: Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200)
- PowerShell: 7.6
- Hermes: install.ps1 (current main)
- Account: local admin
- UAC: elevated

items.title: [Bug]: web_server.py: dashboard action subprocesses become zombies — _ACTION_PROCS uses .poll() but never .wait()

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

After running Hermes a while I noticed zombie processes. Analysis is below, done using Sonnet 4.6.

---

Here's the updated report with the duplicate-check context added:

---

**Title:** `web_server.py`: dashboard action subprocesses become zombies — `_ACTION_PROCS` uses `.poll()` but never `.wait()`

**Labels:** `bug`, `process-management`

---

## Summary

Subprocess handles stored in `_ACTION_PROCS` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`) are never reaped. Processes that exit between status polls accumulate as `<defunct>` zombie entries in the process table, causing resource bloat and incorrect liveness reporting.

## Steps to reproduce

Start the web server, trigger one or more dashboard actions (update, restart, etc.), allow them to complete, then check:

```bash
ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm | grep ' Z '
```

Zombie entries will be children of the web server PID.

## Root cause

`_spawn_hermes_action()` (line ~1070) spawns subprocesses with `start_new_session=True` and stores the `Popen` handle in the module-level `_ACTION_PROCS` dict. The status endpoint calls only `proc.poll()` on these handles:

```python
exit_code = proc.poll()   # reads exit code but does NOT reap the child
```

On Linux, `.poll()` calls `waitpid(WNOHANG)` internally and returns the exit code, but the kernel retains the process table entry until a blocking `waitpid()` is issued. No shutdown or cleanup path in `web_server.py` walks `_ACTION_PROCS` and calls `.wait()`, so every completed action process remains as a zombie for the lifetime of the web server.

## Secondary bug — `meet_bot.py` `pcm_pump` not cleaned up

`plugins/google_meet/meet_bot.py` spawns a `paplay`/`ffmpeg` subprocess stored as `rt["pcm_pump"]` (lines 351, 390). The `run_bot()` cleanup block tears down the speaker thread, realtime session, and audio bridge, but never calls `rt["pcm_pump"].terminate()` / `.wait()`. This process leaks on every normal bot exit.

## Suggested fixes

**`web_server.py`:** After `proc.poll()` returns a non-`None` exit code, reap the child:

```python
exit_code = proc.poll()
if exit_code is not None:
    try:
        proc.wait(timeout=1)   # reap — clears the zombie entry
    except Exception:
        pass
    _ACTION_PROCS.pop(name, None)
    _ACTION_RESULTS[name] = {"exit_code": exit_code, "pid": proc.pid}
```

**`meet_bot.py`:** Add `pcm_pump` to the cleanup block alongside the existing speaker thread / bridge teardown:

```python
if rt.get("pcm_pump"):
    try:
        rt["pcm_pump"].terminate()
        rt["pcm_pump"].wait(timeout=3)
    except Exception:
        pass
```

## Prior art / not a duplicate

- **#6908** — covers `terminal(background=true)` zombies inside Docker sandbox containers (PID 1 not an init process + `process_registry.py`). Closed and fixed. This issue is a different code path entirely: `web_server.py` dashboard actions and `meet_bot.py` audio subprocesses, which are not sandboxed and not covered by the #6908 fix.
- **#28686** — "session in zombie state" refers to a stuck gateway session slot, not OS-level defunct processes. Unrelated.
- **#7131** — `AIAgent.close()` zombie accumulation on long-running gateway deployments. Related class of bug; the reaper thread pattern from that fix is the model for the `_ACTION_PROCS` fix above.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. run hermes gateway for extended period of time (almost a week in my case).

### Expected Behavior

Don't see any zombies.

### Actual Behavior

Noticed three zombie processes.

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Bug Description

On macOS with multiple Hermes profiles installed as launchd services, hermes update appears to restart only the current/default launchd service, not all profile LaunchAgents, despite the update code explicitly saying it should restart all gateways.

The affected machine has several profile LaunchAgents:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
- `ai.hermes.gateway`
- `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-a>`
- `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-b>`
- `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-c>`
- `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-d>`

All of these profile gateways use the same updated Hermes codebase. After hermes update, each running gateway should be restarted so it picks up the new code.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS, install multiple Hermes profile gateways as launchd services:
- `default`
- `<profile-a>`
- `<profile-b>`
- `<profile-c>`
- `<profile-d>`

2. Confirm the services exist:
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist

3. Confirm multiple gateways are running:
ps -axo pid,ppid,command | grep -i '[h]ermes' | grep -i gateway

4. Run:
hermes update

5. Check which launchd services / gateway PIDs were restarted.

6. Observe that the update flow restarts the current/default launchd label but does not enumerate and restart every profile LaunchAgent.

### Expected Behavior

`hermes update` should restart every running gateway that uses the updated shared codebase, including macOS profile LaunchAgents:
- `ai.hermes.gateway`
- `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile>`

This matches the intent documented in hermes_cli/main.py:
"Auto-restart ALL gateways after update.
The code update (git pull) is shared across all profiles, so every running gateway needs restarting to pick up the new code."

### Actual Behavior

On macOS launchd, the update flow appears to restart only the launchd label for the active/current profile via `get_launchd_label()`.

Profile LaunchAgents such as `ai.hermes.gateway-sport`, `ai.hermes.gateway-gaming`, `ai.hermes.gateway-tiny`, and `ai.hermes.gateway-wikilibriste` are not explicitly enumerated and restarted.

The later manual/non-service gateway cleanup path can exclude launchd-managed PIDs via `_get_service_pids()`, so profile gateways managed by launchd may be neither restarted through launchd enumeration nor handled as manual gateways.

**Result**: profile gateways can remain running on pre-update code until manually restarted.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

```shell
Gateway services: default launchd service plus multiple profile launchd services matching `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile>`
```

macOS 26.5.1 (Build 25F80)

### Python Version

3.11.15

0.15.1

```shell
Observed launchd services:
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-a>.plist
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-b>.plist
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-c>.plist
~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway-<profile-d>.plist

Observed running gateway processes:
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main --profile <profile-a> gateway run --replace
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main --profile <profile-b> gateway run --replace
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main --profile <profile-c> gateway run --replace

       ✓ <profile-b>
       ✓ <profile-c>
       ✓ <profile-d>
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The issue appears to be in `hermes_cli/main.py` inside the cmd_update gateway restart flow.

The code comment says:
"Auto-restart ALL gateways after update.
The code update (git pull) is shared across all profiles, so every running gateway needs restarting to pick up the new code."

The flow imports:
- find_gateway_pids(..., all_profiles=True)
- find_profile_gateway_processes
- _get_service_pids
- _graceful_restart_via_sigusr1

So the intended behavior is clearly all-profile restart.

Possible sources:
- ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway*.plist
- launchctl list entries matching ai.hermes.gateway
- Hermes profile registry, resolving each profile's launchd label under that profile context

Then restart each service-managed gateway exactly once.

The restart flow should preserve the existing `_get_service_pids()` exclusion so manually discovered process cleanup does not kill freshly restarted launchd-managed gateways.

## Feature Description

The Desktop App (Electron, `apps/desktop/`) has a hardcoded whitelist of slash commands and does not support skill-based slash commands like `/plan`.

In contrast, both the CLI and TUI automatically register installed skills as slash commands. The TUI handles this through a fallback chain: `slash.exec` → `command.dispatch` → skill scan → load skill payload.

## Current Behavior

In the Desktop App, typing `/plan` (or any skill command) results in it being treated as a plain text message sent to the agent, because:

1. `desktop-slash-commands.ts` defines a fixed `DESKTOP_COMMANDS` set (line 25-45) — `/plan` is not included
2. `isDesktopSlashCommand()` (line 142-151) returns `false` for known-but-unlisted commands
3. There is no `command.dispatch` fallback to scan skill commands like the TUI has

## Motivation

The `/plan` skill is a commonly used workflow (plan before execute). Desktop App users lose this capability with no obvious workaround. Other skill commands (any installed skill that auto-registers as a slash command) are similarly inaccessible.

## Proposed Solution

Port the TUI's skill command fallback to the Desktop App:

1. When an unrecognized slash command is entered, call the gateway's `command.dispatch` RPC (same as TUI does)
2. If the response has `type: 'skill'`, load the skill payload and send it as a user message
3. This would automatically support all installed skill commands without maintaining a separate whitelist

The TUI implementation is in `tui_gateway/server.py` (the `command.dispatch` handler at line 5802) and `ui-tui/src/app/createSlashHandler.ts` (the fallback chain).

## Alternatives Considered

- Adding skill commands to `DESKTOP_COMMANDS` manually — doesn't scale, breaks when skills are added/removed
- Telling users to use CLI/TUI — poor UX for Desktop App users

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop App (Electron)
- macOS (likely affects all platforms)

items.title: [Bug]: Docker/Unraid — HERMES_UID below 1000 (e.g. 99) silently ignored on current main; #32559 fix covered env propagation only, plus pairing/ excluded from chown
items.body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #32559 (closed as completed via #32412). #32412 correctly fixed the s6-overlay **env-propagation** half of that bug — a valid `HERMES_UID` now remaps. But the original Unraid symptom (`HERMES_UID=99`) **still reproduces on the current image** because of a *different* root cause that #32412 never targeted: the `validate_uid_gid` floor requires `id >= 1000`, so Unraid's conventional `99/100` is rejected and the runtime falls back to UID `10000`. A second, related defect (`pairing/` excluded from ownership reconciliation) produces the user-visible `telegram-approved.json` permission error.

### Environment

- Image: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:main` (identical digest to `:latest`), `sha256:bedaa680898269ec1686a085fec144c0b762aade7c7d30fde3ec8044bbdb8410`, **built 2026-06-03T06:51:08Z** (i.e. post-#32412 — it includes the `#!/command/with-contenv sh` cont-init wrapper).
- Command: `gateway run`
- Reproduced in a clean container environment; originally hitting Unraid users (UID 99 / GID 100).

### Bug 1 — `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` below 1000 are silently ignored

`docker/stage2-hook.sh:42`:

```sh
validate_uid_gid() {
    case "$1" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
        *) [ "$1" -ge 1000 ] && [ "$1" -le 65534 ] ;;
    esac
}
```

Evidence on the same image / same boot path:

```bash
# Valid UID >= 1000 -> remap fires, confirming #32412 env propagation works:
docker run -d -e HERMES_UID=5000 -e HERMES_GID=5000 -v v1:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent:main gateway run
docker exec <c> id hermes      # -> uid=5000(hermes) gid=5000(hermes)
#   log: "[stage2] Changing hermes UID to 5000"

# Unraid's 99 -> rejected by the >=1000 floor, falls back to 10000:
docker run -d -e HERMES_UID=99 -e HERMES_GID=100 -v v2:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent:main gateway run
docker exec <c> id hermes      # -> uid=10000(hermes) gid=10000(hermes)
#   no "[stage2] Changing hermes UID" line is logged
```

This contradicts the `uid=99(hermes)` confirmation that #32559's close was based on — it does not reproduce on this digest. I suspect that run didn't actually hit the floor.

**Impact:** Unraid's standard appdata owner is `nobody:users` = `99:100`. Since the runtime ends up as UID `10000` while appdata is owned by `99:100`, writes into `/opt/data` fail — this is the `gateway_state.json` PermissionError tracked in #32559.

**Ask:** Is the `< 1000` floor intentional? The `PUID`/`PGID` docs imply NAS conventions (incl. Unraid's 99/100) are supported, which isn't currently true. Either lower/remove the lower bound (low NAS UIDs like 99 are legitimate), or document that Unraid/NAS users must choose a UID `>= 1000` and `chown` appdata to match.

### Bug 2 — `pairing/` excluded from ownership reconciliation

Even when the runtime is `10000`, `stage2-hook.sh` reconciles `/opt/data` plus a fixed subdir list (`cron sessions logs hooks memories skills skins plans workspace home profiles`) and a few explicit files, but **`pairing/` is deliberately excluded** (#19788, to avoid clobbering host-mounted files). So a pre-existing `/opt/data/pairing` owned by a different UID stays unwritable:

```bash
docker volume create v
docker run --rm --user 0 -v v:/d --entrypoint chown nousresearch/hermes-agent:main -R 99:100 /d  # simulate prior/host ownership
docker run -d --name c -e HERMES_UID=99 -e HERMES_GID=100 -v v:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent:main gateway run
docker exec c stat -c '%u:%g %n' /opt/data /opt/data/pairing
#   -> 10000:10000 /opt/data        (reconciled)
#   -> 99:100      /opt/data/pairing (NOT reconciled)
docker exec -u 10000 c sh -c 'echo x > /opt/data/pairing/telegram-approved.json'
#   sh: cannot create /opt/data/pairing/telegram-approved.json: Permission denied
```

This reproduces the exact error Unraid users hit when running `hermes setup` to pair Telegram:
`PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/opt/data/pairing/telegram-approved.json'`
— reported on the Unraid Community Apps support thread for this template: https://forums.unraid.net/topic/199030-support-medzin-hermes-agent/ . (#10270 is the same root cause from the root-created-file direction.)

**Ask:** add `pairing` to the reconciled-subdir set, or `chown` it to the resolved runtime UID whenever the parent is reconciled.

### Workaround for affected users (Unraid)

Set `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` to a value `>= 1000` (the default `10000` works) and fix appdata ownership on the host:

```bash
chown -R 10000:10000 /mnt/cache/appdata/hermes-agent   # the 'pairing' subfolder especially
```

items.title: [Windows] Clipboard paste mangles emoji to ?? due to PowerShell -NoProfile bypassing UTF-8 encoding
items.body:
## Platform
Windows 11, PowerShell 7, Windows Terminal

## Hermes version
v0.15.1+ (bleeding-edge main, 545 commits past v2026.5.29.2)

## Description
Pasting emoji into the Hermes TUI composer shows `??` instead of the actual emoji. Basic emoji used to work via the fast-echo path, now removed/changed by PR #26011; extended emoji (`🫶` `🫠` `🩷`) never did.

Only affects the Hermes TUI — pasting the same emoji into a regular PowerShell 7 session in Windows Terminal works perfectly.

## Root cause
`ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts` reads the clipboard with:

```bash
powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command Get-Clipboard -Raw
```

The `-NoProfile` flag bypasses the user's PowerShell profile, where UTF-8 encoding may be configured. PowerShell then defaults to the system ANSI code page and emits emoji as `??`.

Verified by running the same command with and without forced UTF-8 encoding: without it, the output bytes are literal `3f 3f` (`??`). With UTF-8 forced inside the `-Command` string, the bytes are proper UTF-8 (`f0 9f ...`).

## Suggested fix
Prefix the `Get-Clipboard` command with UTF-8 encoding setup:

```typescript
const POWERSHELL_GET_CLIPBOARD_SCRIPT =
  "[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new();" +
  "[Console]::InputEncoding=[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new();" +
  "$OutputEncoding=[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new();" +
  'Get-Clipboard -Raw'
```

This matches the approach already used in the write path: `_powershellWriteScript` uses base64 encoding to avoid the same stdin-encoding issue.

## Local verification
Patched locally and verified:

```bash
cd ui-tui
npx vitest run src/__tests__/clipboard.test.ts
# ✓ 19 tests passed

npm run build
# built ui-tui/dist/entry.js
```

items.body:
## Bug description

In Hermes Desktop 0.15.1, pasted images in the chat composer are saved to the Desktop client's local user data directory and then sent to the gateway as local filesystem paths. When Desktop is connected to a remote gateway, the gateway tries to resolve those client-local paths on the remote machine and `image.attach` fails because the file does not exist there.

This makes clipboard image paste unusable in Desktop remote-gateway sessions.

## Environment

- Client: `hermes-desktop` 0.15.1
- Gateway: remote Hermes gateway running on another host
- Observed client path shape: `/home/<desktop-user>/.config/Hermes/composer-images/composer_...png`
- Gateway host does not have that client-local path

## What happens internally

The Desktop chat pane appears to use a path-based attachment flow:

1. The renderer paste handler extracts image blobs from `clipboardData`.
2. It calls `window.hermesDesktop.saveImageBuffer(...)` for pasted image blobs.
3. Electron writes the image under Desktop's local user data directory:
   - `app.getPath('userData')/composer-images/composer_...png`
4. Electron returns the local path.
5. The composer stores the attachment as:
   - `{ kind: "image", path: localPath }`
6. On send, the chat controller calls gateway RPC `image.attach` with that path before `prompt.submit`.
7. In remote-gateway mode, `image.attach` executes on the remote gateway host, so it tries to resolve the client-local path on the remote filesystem.
8. The path does not exist there, so attachment fails.

The relevant built artifact locations from the 0.15.1 Desktop package:

- Electron bridge is path-based, not upload-based:
  - `/nix/store/dc79scvljnaydrxnprp4xq2i1cjmd5v9-hermes-desktop-0.15.1/share/hermes-desktop/electron/preload.cjs:18`
- Clipboard paste writes a local PNG and returns the local path:
  - `/nix/store/dc79scvljnaydrxnprp4xq2i1cjmd5v9-hermes-desktop-0.15.1/share/hermes-desktop/electron/main.cjs:3702`
- The local write happens under `app.getPath('userData')/composer-images/...`:
  - `/nix/store/dc79scvljnaydrxnprp4xq2i1cjmd5v9-hermes-desktop-0.15.1/share/hermes-desktop/electron/main.cjs:2442`

## Expected behavior

Pasting an image into Desktop should work both with local and remote gateways. In remote-gateway mode, the gateway should receive image bytes or a gateway-readable stored file path, not a Desktop-client-local path.

## Actual behavior

Desktop sends a local filesystem path like `/home/<desktop-user>/.config/Hermes/composer-images/...png` to `image.attach`. The remote gateway runs on another host and cannot read that path.

## Suggested fixes

Any of these would solve the class of bug:

1. Desktop detects remote-gateway mode, uploads image bytes to the backend, then attaches the returned backend-side path.
2. Gateway exposes an RPC such as `image.upload` that accepts bytes or base64, stores the file under the remote Hermes image directory, and returns a remote-readable attachment handle/path.
3. Short-term workaround: manually copy the image to the gateway host first and attach the remote path, but Desktop should not require this for clipboard paste.

## Impact

This breaks a core UX path for users running Desktop against a remote Hermes gateway: paste screenshot/image into chat, then send it for vision or multimodal workflows.

items.title: WeChat typing indicator stuck permanently after long agent sessions
items.body:
## Describe the bug

When an agent session on WeChat (iLink) exceeds ~10 minutes, the typing
indicator (". . . 正在输入") becomes permanently stuck on the client side
and never clears — even after the agent has finished responding and
delivered the message.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Trigger a long-running agent task on WeChat (e.g. hyperframes video
   rendering, long tool chains, background approval waits)
2. Wait for the session to exceed ~10 minutes
3. Observe: the typing indicator remains after the response is delivered

## Expected behavior

The typing indicator should clear immediately after the agent finishes
responding.

## Root cause

The WeChat iLink `typing_ticket` (obtained from `getConfig`) has a
600-second TTL in the `TypingTicketCache`. When the session exceeds this
duration:

1. `send_typing` silently returns (ticket is `None`)
2. `stop_typing` silently returns (ticket is `None`)
3. The `TYPING_STOP=2` signal is **never sent** to iLink
4. The WeChat client keeps showing the typing indicator indefinitely

The only way to clear it is to send a new message (which triggers a
fresh `getConfig` call and a new ticket).

## Proposed fix

See PR #38082 — adds `_ensure_typing_ticket()` that transparently
refreshes the ticket when the cached one has expired, so both
`send_typing` and `stop_typing` can always obtain a valid ticket.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: main @ 64202200a
- Platform: WeChat iLink
- WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux)

items.title: [Bug]: main branch reports 0.15.1 after v2026.5.29.2 release

items.body:
## Bug Description

The current `main` branch reports Hermes Agent version `0.15.1` in both `pyproject.toml` and `hermes_cli/__init__.py`, even though the latest published release tag `v2026.5.29.2` reports `0.15.2` and `main` contains newer commits after that release.

This makes Git/source installs that correctly track `origin/main` look stale or downgraded when users run `hermes --version`, even when their checkout is actually up to date with `origin/main`.

Related PR: #35524. That PR appears to fix the metadata, but there does not appear to be a canonical issue tracking the underlying bug. If that PR is closed/replaced, the bug should still remain tracked.

This is not the same as #35070 / #35142: in this case `pyproject.toml` and `hermes_cli/__init__.py` are internally consistent on `main`; they are both behind the latest release tag metadata.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect `main` metadata:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/pyproject.toml | grep '^version'
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/hermes_cli/__init__.py | grep '__version__\|__release_date__'
```

2. Inspect the latest release tag metadata:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/v2026.5.29.2/pyproject.toml | grep '^version'
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/v2026.5.29.2/hermes_cli/__init__.py | grep '__version__\|__release_date__'
```

3. Compare `main` against the tag:

```bash
git ls-remote https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git refs/heads/main 'refs/tags/v2026.5.29.2^{}'
```

## Expected Behavior

A Git/source install that tracks the current `main` branch should not report an older package/runtime version than the latest published release tag after release commits have landed.

At minimum, `hermes --version` should make Git/main build identity clear enough that an up-to-date `origin/main` checkout does not look older than the latest release.

## Actual Behavior

At the time of this report:

```text
main pyproject.toml:            version = "0.15.1"
main hermes_cli/__init__.py:    __version__ = "0.15.1"
main hermes_cli/__init__.py:    __release_date__ = "2026.5.29"

tag v2026.5.29.2 pyproject.toml:         version = "0.15.2"
tag v2026.5.29.2 hermes_cli/__init__.py: __version__ = "0.15.2"
tag v2026.5.29.2 hermes_cli/__init__.py: __release_date__ = "2026.5.29.2"
```

Also at the time of this report:

```text
origin/main:              64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818
v2026.5.29.2 peeled tag:  77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5
```

So `main` has advanced beyond the release tag, but still reports the older version metadata.

## Affected Component

- Setup / Installation
- CLI

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

N/A - this is reproducible from public upstream repository metadata and raw files. No local logs or credentials are required to reproduce.

## Operating System

macOS 15.x, but this is not OS-specific. The reproduction is against upstream repository files.

## Python Version

N/A - repository metadata issue.

## Hermes Version

`main` reports `0.15.1`; latest release tag `v2026.5.29.2` reports `0.15.2`.

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

N/A.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The release tag `v2026.5.29.2` contains the expected version metadata, but `main` currently has both `pyproject.toml` and `hermes_cli/__init__.py` set to `0.15.1` / `2026.5.29`.

Because both files agree on `main`, the version consistency check added by #35142 likely does not flag this case. The issue is not file-to-file drift within a checkout; it is stale branch metadata relative to the latest release tag.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

Either:

1. Merge #35524 or equivalent to sync `main` metadata to `0.15.2` / `2026.5.29.2`, including `pyproject.toml`, `hermes_cli/__init__.py`, and `acp_registry/agent.json`; or
2. Adjust Git/source install version reporting so `hermes --version` includes commit SHA/build identity and cannot make an up-to-date `origin/main` checkout appear older than the latest tag.

## Existing Related Work

- Related PR: #35524
- Related but not duplicate: #35070 / #35142
- Related but not duplicate: #35857
- Related but not duplicate: #36743

items.title: [Bug]: TUI slash worker subprocesses leak after session close, accumulating zombie processes
items.body:
## Bug Description

When a TUI session is closed (user exits Hermes or closes the TUI tab), the `_SlashWorker` subprocess spawned during `_init_session()` is **not cleaned up**. These orphaned processes accumulate every time the TUI is opened and closed while the dashboard process remains running.

**Observed on user machine:** 5 zombie slash workers, each ~13MB RSS, two sharing the same `session-key` (indicating `_restart_slash_worker` also leaks — old process not killed before starting a new one).

### Zombie processes found:
```
PID    RSS %MEM ELAPSED  COMMAND
83740  12896  0.1 01:02:27 python -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260602_182842_28ddd6
83743  12896  0.1 01:02:27 python -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260602_173931_fb4c4970
83752  12880  0.1 01:02:12 python -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260602_182842_28ddd6
83758  12896  0.1 01:02:07 python -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260602_172321_13f22a4e
83764  12896  0.1 01:02:04 python -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260602_170252_75c29b
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes` (opens TUI) — a `_SlashWorker` subprocess is spawned
2. Use any `/` slash command
3. Close the TUI (Ctrl+C, or close the terminal tab)
4. Repeat steps 1-3 several times
5. Run `ps aux | grep slash_worker` — orphaned workers remain

## Root Cause

`_finalize_session()` in `tui_gateway/server.py:287` does not close the `slash_worker` subprocess:

```python
def _finalize_session(session, end_reason="tui_close"):
    ...
    # Commits memory and updates DB, but does NOT close session["slash_worker"]
```

The slash worker IS properly closed in:
- `session.close` JSON-RPC handler (line 3502-3527) ✅ — calls `_finalize_session()` first, then separately closes worker
- `_shutdown_sessions()` (line 326-334) ✅ — but only runs when dashboard exits

But `_finalize_session()` itself does NOT close the worker — so any code path that calls `_finalize_session()` without separately handling the worker will leak.

Additionally, two workers with the **same session-key** (`20260602_182842_28ddd6`) were observed alive simultaneously, suggesting `_restart_slash_worker()` may also leak under certain conditions.

## Expected Behavior

When a TUI session ends, the associated `_SlashWorker` subprocess should be reliably terminated.

## Proposed Fix

In `_finalize_session()`, add slash worker cleanup:

```python
def _finalize_session(session, end_reason="tui_close"):
    ...
    worker = session.get("slash_worker")
    if worker:
        try:
            worker.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
```

Also consider making `_SlashWorker.close()` more robust (longer `wait()` timeout, fallback `kill()`) and adding a guard against concurrent `_restart_slash_worker` calls.

## Environment
- Hermes: v0.15.1 / v0.15.2
- OS: macOS
- Python: 3.11.15

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway silently drops safe local MEDIA files from working dirs (e.g. /root) instead of staging them
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the agent emits a `MEDIA:<absolute path>` directive for a deliverable it produced in a normal working directory, the gateway can silently drop the attachment while the chat reply still claims a file is attached. The user sees text like "Here is your proposal" with nothing attached.

`gateway/platforms/base.py::validate_media_delivery_path` only accepts files that are either under a Hermes cache root, under an operator-allowlisted root (`HERMES_MEDIA_ALLOW_DIRS`), or (in strict mode) freshly produced. In the default non-strict mode it accepts anything not on the credential/system denylist, but that denylist includes the whole `/root` prefix. So when the gateway runs as root (common in Docker), the operator's home and working directory is `/root`, and every deliverable under it is rejected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway as root (so `$HOME=/root`), default config (non-strict).
2. Ask the agent to generate a document; it writes e.g. `/root/clawd/proposal.docx` (or any `/root/work/...` path).
3. The agent replies with `MEDIA:/root/clawd/proposal.docx`.
4. No file attaches. `gateway.log` shows:
   `Skipping unsafe MEDIA directive path: /root/clawd/proposal.docx`
5. Copy the same file to `~/.hermes/cache/documents/proposal.docx` and send that path instead. It delivers.

## Expected Behavior

A safe, freshly produced local deliverable should be delivered, without the operator having to hand-copy it into a cache directory, and without broadly allowlisting `/root`, `Path.home()`, or arbitrary working dirs.

## Actual Behavior

The file is silently dropped. The user gets a false-success message (text says a file is attached; nothing is). Only the operator can diagnose it, and only from `gateway.log`.

## Affected Component

gateway / platforms (MEDIA delivery)

## Proposed Fix

Stage the requested file into the matching Hermes media cache (which is already allowlisted) and deliver the staged copy, while keeping the full credential/system denylist intact (refuse `/etc`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.hermes/.env`, credential filenames like `.netrc`/`id_rsa`/`*.pem`, resolve symlinks first, and in strict mode only stage freshly produced files). The only relaxation is allowing the running user's own home (so a root-run gateway can deliver `/root/work/proposal.docx` while `/root/.ssh` stays blocked).

## Related

- #34485 (merged) improved diagnosable MEDIA rejection logging and canonical cache roots, but did not address working-dir deliverables.
- #32644, #13356: attachments report success but never arrive.
- #34178, #32054, #32880, #31864: surfacing dropped/rejected MEDIA attachments (mostly the send_message path / visible feedback).

items.title: Remote gateway (macOS): desktop session won't hold — gateway SIGTERM → WebSocket close 1012 loop; "Test remote" false-passes; auto-updater corrupts install

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, connecting **Hermes Desktop in "remote gateway" mode** to a Hermes backend running as the always-on `ai.hermes.gateway` launchd service never produces a stable session. REST succeeds (the version shows, **Test remote passes**), but the desktop ends on **"Hermes couldn't start — The background gateway didn't come up / Could not connect to Hermes gateway."**

Server-side logs show the dashboard WebSocket is **accepted and then dropped with close code 1012 ("service restart")**, correlating with the gateway service being SIGTERM'd and relaunched. So the handshake/auth/origin are fine — the gateway underneath simply doesn't stay up long enough for the desktop to hold a session.

Separately, the desktop **auto-updater left the install corrupted** (`hermes-setup --update` is SIGKILLed, in-app "Repair install" doesn't recover), which required a manual reinstall.

This looks related to (but broader than) #35322 and #18415.

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent / gateway:** v0.15.1 (2026.5.29), upstream `a429a2a0`
- **Hermes Desktop:** 0.15.1 era
- **Backend host:** Mac Studio, macOS, Apple Silicon — Hermes installed as a launchd **user agent** (`ai.hermes.gateway`)
- **Client host:** MacBook Pro, macOS — Hermes Desktop
- **Inference:** custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama on the Studio, `qwen3.6:27b-mlx`)
- **Connection path:** SSH tunnel `ssh -N <user>@<studio-ip> -L 127.0.0.1:9119:127.0.0.1:9119`, desktop pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:9119` (tunnel used because a direct LAN URL is rejected — see #35322)

## Steps to reproduce

1. On the backend host, run Hermes as the `ai.hermes.gateway` launchd service (`python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`).
2. Serve the dashboard with the chat WebSocket: `hermes dashboard --tui --skip-build --no-open` (defaults to `127.0.0.1:9119`).
3. From the client, open an SSH tunnel: `ssh -N <user>@<studio-ip> -L 127.0.0.1:9119:127.0.0.1:9119`.
4. In Hermes Desktop → Settings → Gateway: select **Remote gateway**, Remote URL `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, paste the dashboard session token.
5. Click **Test remote** → passes ("Connected to http://127.0.0.1:9119 · Hermes 0.15.1").
6. Click **Save and reconnect**.

## Expected

The desktop holds a live session against the remote gateway.

## Actual

- Desktop shows **"Hermes couldn't start — The background gateway didn't come up / Could not connect to Hermes gateway."**
- **Test remote passes** every time regardless (it appears to validate only REST, not the gateway WebSocket), so it is a misleading green light.
- The desktop's own recent-logs panel shows it stuck during boot at `Finding an open local port` → `Resolving Hermes…` (note: even in **remote** mode the desktop boots a **local** backend first — `Starting Hermes backend via Hermes at /Users/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent` — and the whole flow is gated on that).

## Evidence (server-side, backend host)

**`~/.hermes/logs/gui.log`** — WebSocket is accepted, then dropped with code 1012:

```
tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:<port>
tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:<port> reason=client_disconnect(code=1012,reason=) messages=10 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=0 detached_sessions=0
```

**`~/.hermes/logs/gateway.error.log`** — gateway repeatedly terminated by SIGTERM:

```
gateway.run: Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1 parent_name=? loadavg_1m=...
gateway.platforms.whatsapp: WhatsApp is enabled but not paired ... Run `hermes whatsapp` to pair, or remove WHATSAPP_ENABLED ...
gateway.run: ✗ whatsapp failed to connect
(repeats)
```

**`launchctl list | grep -i hermes`** — service's last exit status is `-15` (SIGTERM):

```
57938 -15 ai.hermes.gateway
```

**`~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`** — gateway/api_server itself comes up cleanly on a separate port (`8642`), so the agent is healthy; only the desktop session won't persist:

```
gateway.platforms.api_server: API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:8642 (model: hermes-agent)
gateway.run: Gateway running with 3 platform(s)
```

## Suspected root causes / discussion

1. **The gateway service cycles and takes the desktop WebSocket down with it (1012).** The 1012 closes line up with `ai.hermes.gateway` being SIGTERM'd/relaunched. Whatever is bouncing the service (launchd KeepAlive on a transient failure, the `--replace` semantics, the unpaired-WhatsApp failure path, or load) makes a stable remote desktop session impossible. The desktop reports this as a hard "could not connect to gateway" rather than a recoverable reconnect.
2. **On native macOS, `gateway run` cannot serve the dashboard.** Per `gateway run --help`, the supervised-dashboard behaviour (`HERMES_DASHBOARD`) only applies inside the s6/Docker image. So a launchd-service deployment must run `hermes dashboard` as a *second* process, and the desktop's remote mode depends on that dashboard's `--tui` PTY WebSocket. This two-process split on macOS isn't documented and is easy to get into a conflicting/unstable state. A documented, supported "always-on dashboard + gateway" story for native macOS (e.g. a `--dashboard`/`--tui` flag on `gateway run`, or an official launchd plist) would remove the foot-guns.
3. **"Test remote" is a false positive.** It passes while the gateway WebSocket never holds, which is exactly the "works in tests but not in practice" symptom others have reported. Test remote should also exercise the gateway WebSocket.

## Secondary issue: desktop auto-updater corrupts the install

After an auto-update, the desktop was stuck on "Hermes couldn't start." Recovery tooling was itself broken:

- `~/.hermes/hermes-setup --update` → `zsh: killed` (SIGKILL — damaged or invalidly-signed binary).
- In-app **"Repair install"** did not recover; boot stayed hung at `Resolving Hermes…`.
- A dock duplicate appeared and the original app icon became a broken-alias "?".
- A **manual reinstall** of `Hermes.app` was required. After reinstall, **local gateway works**, but **remote still fails** as above.

Suggested: the updater should verify the downloaded binary's signature/integrity and roll back cleanly on a failed update, and "Repair install" should detect/replace a SIGKILLed/damaged `hermes-setup`.

## Suggested fixes (summary)

- Stop the gateway service from cycling out from under an active desktop session, and have the desktop **reconnect** on a 1012 rather than hard-failing.
- Make **Test remote** validate the gateway WebSocket, not just REST.
- Document (or provide a flag for) a stable **gateway + dashboard** native-macOS/launchd deployment.
- Harden the **auto-updater** (integrity check + rollback) and make **Repair install** recover a damaged `hermes-setup`.

items.title: Windows Desktop update can loop after dirty bundled repo checkout and broken venv

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: python:uv
labels.description: Pull requests that update python:uv code

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop on Windows can get stuck in a recovery loop after a failed update. In this case, bootstrap failed at the `repository` stage because the bundled install repo had local working-tree changes, so `git checkout <target commit>` refused to proceed. After retry/repair, Desktop then adopted the existing install and attempted to start the backend from `hermes-agent\venv`, but that venv was effectively broken/empty and crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`.

This looked recoverable manually by resetting the bundled install repo, checking out the target commit, recreating the launcher venv, and reinstalling Hermes dependencies into that venv. It seems like the Desktop repair/update path should do some version of this automatically, or at least detect and present an actionable recovery.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Install path pattern: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`
- Hermes target commit from bootstrap: `64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818`
- Previous installed commit observed: `43fd63b4b50c931889051f05783d9cb572bf6ae4`
- Python: `3.11.15`
- Git: `2.53.0.windows.1`
- uv: `0.11.18`

## Observed behavior

Desktop shows:

```text
Hermes couldn't start
The background gateway didn't come up.
Error invoking remote method 'hermes:connection': Error: Hermes bootstrap failed at stage 'repository': git checkout 64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818 failed (exit 1).
```

Relevant log excerpt:

```text
[bootstrap] stage repository running
-> Existing installation found, updating...
From https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent
 * branch 64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818 -> FETCH_HEAD
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
	.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml
Please commit your changes or stash them before you switch branches.
Aborting
Hermes bootstrap failed at stage 'repository': git checkout 64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818 failed (exit 1)
```

After retry/repair, Desktop attempted to adopt the existing install and start the backend, then failed with:

```text
Starting Hermes backend via Hermes at %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent (venv: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "...\hermes_cli\config.py", line 226, in <module>
    import yaml
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1).
```

## Diagnostics

The bundled repo had a dirty working tree. The specific file named by the bootstrap failure did not show semantic changes, only line-ending churn:

```text
git diff -- .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml
warning: in the working copy of '.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
```

`git diff --stat` showed many tracked files modified/deleted, including large deletions under `apps/desktop` and `apps/bootstrap-installer`, suggesting the install checkout was left in a stale or partial update state.

`venv\Scripts` only contained `python.exe`, and invoking the launcher venv failed to import `yaml`.

## Manual recovery that worked

From `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`:

```powershell
git config core.autocrlf false
git reset --hard HEAD
git checkout 64202200a6043b685750e16107067971446f8818
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\uv.exe venv --clear %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv --python 3.11
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\uv.exe pip install --python %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe -e .
```

After that:

```powershell
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import yaml; import hermes_cli.config; print('imports ok')"
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main --help
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main status
```

All succeeded.

## Expected behavior

The Windows Desktop updater/recovery path should avoid entering a loop when the bundled install repo is dirty due to line-ending churn or a partial previous update. Possible fixes:

- Set repo-local line-ending behavior for the managed install checkout before update operations.
- Treat the managed install directory as disposable app code and hard reset/clean it before checking out the target commit, while preserving Hermes home data such as config, auth, sessions, memories, logs, etc.
- If the venv is missing core dependencies after a repair, recreate/sync the exact launcher venv Desktop will use instead of adopting the install as ready.
- Surface an actionable recovery message if automatic reset/rebuild is not considered safe.

## Privacy note

Paths and user-specific details above are redacted to `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. No config/auth/session data is included.

items.title: [Bug]: Docker Hindsight memory provider loses hindsight-client after container recreate/update
items.body:
### Bug Description

I am running Hermes Agent in Docker using nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest. I configured the native Hindsight memory provider with hermes memory setup in local_external mode, pointing to a self-hosted Hindsight API at http://hindsight:8888.

The Hindsight server itself works correctly, and Hermes profile configs persist correctly under /opt/data/profiles/<profile>/hindsight/config.json. Memory recall/retain works after setup. However, after updating/recreating the Hermes Docker containers, Hindsight recall/retain fails because the Python dependency hindsight-client is missing from /opt/hermes/.venv.

The failure is:

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hindsight_client'

Running this inside the container fixes it temporarily:

uv pip install --python /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python "hindsight-client>=0.4.22"

But because /opt/hermes/.venv is inside the container image layer, the dependency is lost again after Docker image updates/recreates. Hermes also shows a warning that pip install is not officially supported, which makes the durable Docker workflow unclear.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Agent with Docker image nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest.
2. Mount persistent data at /opt/data.
3. Run hermes -p <profile> memory setup.
4. Select/configure Hindsight in local_external mode.
5. Use Hindsight successfully.
6. Recreate/update the Hermes Docker container.
7. Try to use Hindsight recall/retain again.

### Expected Behavior

The native Hindsight memory provider should remain usable after Docker container recreate/update.

Either:

the official Docker image should include the required hindsight-client dependency,
or provider dependencies should be installed into a persistent location under /opt/data,
or the documented Docker workflow should explain the recommended durable way to handle optional memory-provider dependencies.

### Actual Behavior

After container recreate/update, the Hindsight plugin/config is still present and the Hindsight server is still running, but Hermes cannot use Hindsight because hindsight-client is no longer installed in /opt/hermes/.venv.

Example failure:

Failed to search memory: No module named 'hindsight_client'

### Bug Description

In cron jobs, the `memory` tool appears to be available/exposed, but calling it at runtime fails with:

"Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."

This makes cron behavior confusing/inconsistent: the tool is present in the cron toolset, but unusable once invoked.

From local code inspection, cron jobs instantiate `AIAgent(..., skip_memory=True, platform="cron")` in `cron/scheduler.py`, while the cron default toolset (`hermes-cron`) still inherits `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS`, which includes `memory`.

So from a user perspective:
- cron can see/use the `memory` tool in schema
- but the runtime environment disables memory access
- result: tool-call failure instead of either:
  - hiding/removing the tool from cron sessions, or
  - allowing the configured memory provider to work while still skipping prompt-memory injection


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a cron job that explicitly tries to call the `memory` tool.
2. Let the cron job run.
3. Observe that the tool is exposed to the agent, but the call fails at runtime.

Minimal reproduction prompt for a one-shot cron job:
- "Use the memory tool once to save a short fact like 'cron memory probe' to memory, then report the result."

Observed behavior:
- cron run reaches the memory tool
- tool returns:
  "Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."


### Expected Behavior

One of these should happen consistently:

1. If memory is intentionally unsupported in cron sessions:
   - the `memory` tool should not be exposed in cron toolsets/schemas

OR

2. If the configured memory backend should be usable in cron:
   - the tool should work at runtime
   - `skip_memory=True` should only prevent prompt-memory injection / user-representation pollution, not disable the backend entirely


### Actual Behavior

The `memory` tool is exposed in cron sessions, but calling it fails at runtime with:

"Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."


### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/ddcIJ
agent.log    https://paste.rs/aAiwK
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/I6Ouu
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Runtime tool error returned by memory tool:

"Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Likely cause is an inconsistency between cron tool exposure and cron runtime initialization:

1. `toolsets.py`
   - `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` includes `"memory"`
   - `hermes-cron` uses `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS`
   - so cron sessions inherit/expose the memory tool

2. `cron/scheduler.py`
   - cron creates the agent with:
     `skip_memory=True`
   - local inspection showed this around:
     `cron/scheduler.py:1686`

3. `tools/memory_tool.py`

     "Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."
   - local inspection showed this around:
     `tools/memory_tool.py:615`

- either `skip_memory=True` suppresses memory backend initialization too aggressively for cron

- remove/filter the `memory` tool from cron sessions when `skip_memory=True`

Option B:
- keep the tool exposed, but decouple prompt-memory injection from memory-backend availability
- i.e. allow cron to use the configured memory provider while still skipping automatic memory loading into the prompt / user representation

items.title: [Feature]: Desktop update should auto-restart messaging gateway after update completes

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

Every time Hermes Agent is updated via the **Desktop (Electron) app**, the messaging gateway is NOT automatically restarted. This means Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and all other messaging channels go offline immediately after the update and stay dead until the user manually runs `hermes gateway restart`.

This is a significant UX gap because:

1. **Desktop is the primary update path for many users** — the one-click update button in the dashboard is the most convenient way to stay current
2. **Messaging channels are critical infrastructure** — users rely on Telegram/Discord bots for notifications, cron job delivery, and real-time interaction
3. **Silent failure with no notification** — there is zero indication in the Desktop UI that the gateway died; the user only discovers it when they try to message the bot and get no response
4. **The CLI `hermes update` path already handles this** — it auto-restarts gateway services after pulling new code (see `hermes_cli/main.py` ~L3800), so the Desktop path is a strict regression

## Current behavior

1. Desktop shows "Update available" → user clicks Update
2. Update completes, Desktop dashboard reconnects fine
3. Messaging gateway is dead — Telegram bot unresponsive, Discord bot offline, cron delivery fails silently
4. User must open a terminal and manually run `hermes gateway restart`

## Expected behavior

1. Desktop update flow should detect running gateway processes (all profiles)
2. After update completes, auto-restart the gateway with the new code
3. Verify the restarted gateway is healthy (HTTP health check on `:8642` or process status)
4. If restart fails, surface an error in the Desktop UI instead of failing silently

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: latest (updated via Desktop)
- Gateway: Windows Scheduled Task (`Hermes_Gateway_V2`), auto-starts at login via VBS wrapper → pythonw.exe

## Related issues

- #36213 — Windows: `hermes gateway restart` does not verify old process termination (same platform, different code path)
- #6631 — `hermes update` gateway restart does not verify service survived (Linux systemd variant)
- #18409 — PR: auto-restart when source files change (gateway self-detection, but only triggers on inbound message, not on update completion)
- #7503 — PR: drain in-flight work before restart (graceful restart mechanics)

## Suggested fix

The Desktop update handler should mirror what `hermes_cli/main.py` already does post-update:

```
After update completes:
1. find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True)
2. For each PID: graceful stop (SIGTERM / taskkill)
3. Verify old PID is dead (poll with psutil / tasklist)
4. If still alive: force kill (taskkill /F)
5. Start gateway (hermes gateway start or service restart)
6. Verify health (HTTP GET :8642/health or process check)
7. If failed: retry once, then surface error in Desktop UI
```

The key gap is that the Desktop update path (likely in the Electron main process or a renderer IPC handler) does not have the same post-update gateway restart logic that the CLI path has. This should be unified or at minimum the Desktop path should shell out to `hermes gateway restart --all-profiles` after the update completes.

items.title: [Bug]: TUI can pass host launch cwd into Docker terminal sessions on Windows

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description
On Windows, `hermes --tui` can pass the host launch directory into Docker-backed terminal sessions even when no session workspace was explicitly selected.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Hermes to use the Docker terminal backend.
2. Launch `hermes --tui` from a Windows host directory such as `%USERPROFILE%`.
3. In the TUI, ask Hermes to use the terminal tool for a simple command such as `pwd`.

## Expected Behavior
If no session workspace was explicitly selected, TUI mode should not register a terminal cwd override from the gateway's host launch directory. The terminal backend should continue using the configured or default container-safe cwd.

## Actual Behavior
The Docker-backed terminal session is started with a working directory derived from the Windows host launch directory.

That path is not valid inside the container, so terminal commands fail in TUI mode.

## Affected Component
- Terminal UI (TUI)
- Terminal tool
- Docker backend

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)
- N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report
Not attached publicly because the generated debug report includes identifying local filesystem details.

If maintainers want it, I can provide a redacted local debug report produced with `hermes debug share --local`.

## Operating System
Windows 10

## Python Version
3.11.14

## Hermes Version
Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)
No additional traceback to attach here. The failure reproduces reliably from the TUI path when Docker-backed terminal commands are invoked.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)
The TUI startup path appears to propagate the launch directory into terminal cwd handling:

- `hermes_cli/main.py` sets `HERMES_CWD=os.getcwd()` when launching the TUI.
- `ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts` starts the Python gateway child with `cwd = process.env.HERMES_CWD || root`.
- `tui_gateway/server.py` `session.create` falls back to `os.getcwd()` via `_completion_cwd()` when no explicit workspace is provided.
- `tui_gateway/server.py` then registers that implicit session cwd with `tools.terminal_tool.register_task_env_overrides(...)`, which causes Docker terminal sessions to use the host path as `cwd`.

`tui_gateway/server.py` already distinguishes explicit vs implicit session cwd for persistence, so the terminal override path appears to be treating an implicit launch directory as if it were an explicit workspace selection.

## Proposed Fix (optional)
Only register a per-session terminal cwd override when the session cwd was explicitly selected by the user or restored from a stored explicit workspace. An implicit TUI launch directory should not override the Docker backend's configured/default cwd.
